facts: These appeals have been filed by accused persons against the judgment and order dated 16.3.2006 passed by the Madras High Court in Criminal Appeal No.1540 of 2002 by which the High Court has dismissed the appeal filed by the appellants.
The deceased Michaelraj and the accused persons were residents of the same Village in Taluk Udayarapalayam in District Perambalur.
There was a land dispute between Michaelraj and the accused persons on account of which there was enmity between them.
Originally, the grandmother of the deceased Michaelraj executed a settlement deed in favor of Michaelraj which was subsequently cancelled.
Thereafter, a portion of the property was executed in favor of the appellant.
Despite the settlement deed, the appellant claimed that his possession of property was disturbed by the deceased and his relatives.
Therefore, the appellant filed a suit against the deceased and his relatives.

The matter came up before the Trial Court, which after going through the evidence provided by the sole-eyewitness PW-3, concluded that the case of prosecution is proved beyond doubt and thereby convicted the accused under Sections 148, 149, 302 & 341 of IPC.
Aggrieved by the judgment of the Trial Court, the accused preferred an appeal before the Madras High Court.

The High Court vide its judgment and order dated 16.3.2006, partly allowed the appeal filed by the accused persons, convicted them u/s. 304 Part II of IPC and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for five years,
issues: Whether the evidence provided by PW-3 is reliable?
Whether the accused can be convicted on the sole testimony of a single witness?
petitioner_arguments: The entire case of the prosecution rested on the oral evidence provided by an eye-witness, which was rejected by the High Court and simultaneously dismissed by this Court.
In absence of reliable testimony and evidence, guilt of the accused cannot be proved.
It was not given proper materials to examine the nature of the treatment given to the deceased.
respondent_arguments: The impugned judgment passed by the High Court is supported.
court_reasoning: There is no legal impediment in convicting a person on the sole testimony of a single witness provided he is wholly reliable.
A difference between ocular and medical evidence will not stand any ground in acquitting the accused in the present case.
holding: The appeals lack merit and are accordingly dismissed.
